newsitem.title: CHILE: Chilean lawmakers pass harsh statement on Cuba.
newsitem.headline: Chilean lawmakers pass harsh statement on Cuba.

text.p: Chile's lower house of Congress passed a resolution on Wednesday urging democratic rule in Cuba and blasting Cuban leader Fidel Castro three weeks before he is due to visit Chile.

The resolution, proposed by 10 conservative legislators, lashed Cuba for holding "political prisoners" and for not allowing free elections and freedom of the press, and accused it of backing "terrorist delinquents" and guerrillas in Latin America.

"The Chamber of Deputies...expresses our complete solidarity with the Cuban people, who are the main victims of the outrages of Fidel Castro's communist regime," said the resolution, passed by the Chamber of Deputies in Valparaiso.
The resolution faced a draw of 22 to 22, with four abstentions, but on the second ballot the abstentions counted as votes in favour under congressional rules.
The outcome was surprising since, unlike the Senate, the Chamber of Deputies is controlled by lawmakers from Chile's ruling centre-left coalition.

"It is a fact that the Cuban government keeps political prisoners in its jails, using force to prevent the exercising of the most elementary rights of a democratic nation, such as freedom of speech, of labour, of movement and of information," said the resolution.

It criticised the island's government for not allowing "ideological pluralism, the existence of political parties, the periodic election of government and legislative authorities and freedom of the press."
It added that Chile had been "the principal victim of Cuban interventionism," referring to Cuba's alleged support for left-wing guerrillas after the military overturned civilian rule in Chile.

Castro is scheduled to arrive in Chile on Nov. 9 for the sixth Ibero-American Summit, which will bring together the leaders of all Latin American countries plus those of Spain and Portugal. Local supporters and critics of his rule have promised to hold street demonstrations during the summit.
